headline: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine Will Intensify Russian Refinery Strikes
seoTitle: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine Will Intensify Russian Refinery Strikes | FMB News
seoDescription: Ukraine will intensify attacks on Russian oil refineries in response to Moscow's expanded air campaign, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Reuters.
deck: The Ukrainian president described the planned refinery campaign as retaliation for Russia's expanded strikes and said civilian sites would not be targeted.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Reuters in an interview published Saturday, October 3, that Ukraine would intensify attacks on Russian oil refineries in response to what he described as Moscow's expanded campaign against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure.

Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence had obtained documents showing that Russian President Vladimir Putin authorized a broader range of targets ahead of winter. That intelligence assessment was not independently available for review, and the Kremlin did not provide Reuters with a response to the allegation.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Reuters directly interviewed Zelenskyy in Kyiv on October 2 and published his refinery-strike statement at 4:03 p.m. UTC on October 3, or 12:03 a.m. Philippine time on October 4.

Associated Press independently reported that Russia damaged Kyiv's Northern Bridge after two earlier days of attacks had forced full or partial closures of three of the capital's six road bridges. AP also reported that Russia's Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue what it called retaliatory strikes, while Russia's Defense Ministry acknowledged striking the bridge and characterized it as a military logistics route.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: Zelenskyy's claim about a Russian 'new doctrine' rests on intelligence documents that have not been made public. Russia and Ukraine continue to deny deliberately targeting civilians, while independent reporting documents civilian casualties and damage to non-military infrastructure.

No operational timetable, target list or expected scale for the announced Ukrainian refinery campaign was disclosed. Its effect on Russian fuel output, exports or world prices therefore cannot yet be established.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The new statement is an independently newsworthy continuation of the energy-target conflict. FMB News first reported on September 16 that Russia and Ukraine were continuing to hit energy sites despite a proposed truce: https://www.francinemariebautista.com/news/russia-ukraine-energy-strikes-september-15-2026/

Ukraine's presidential office said on September 15 that Kyiv was strengthening protection for critical infrastructure and logistics after reviewing intelligence on Russia's planned targets. On September 25, it also said the government was accelerating interceptor production and protecting communications infrastructure.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The Philippines imports most of its petroleum requirements. A sustained campaign against Russian refineries could tighten diesel and other refined-product markets, affecting international prices that feed into local transport and logistics costs. No immediate Philippine pump-price change can be attributed to this announcement alone.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for independently confirmed refinery strikes, Russian production or export disruptions, official responses from Moscow, and any renewed energy ceasefire proposal. Philippine consumers should also watch subsequent Department of Energy and oil-company price advisories rather than treating battlefield claims as proof of a local price movement.

verificationNotes: Reuters directly interviewed President Zelenskyy; his announced intent is confirmed as a statement, not as proof that future refinery strikes have occurred.
The alleged Russian 'new doctrine' is explicitly attributed to Zelenskyy and Ukrainian intelligence because the underlying documents were not publicly available.
Associated Press independently corroborates the intensified Russian campaign against Kyiv infrastructure and carries official Russian descriptions of the bridge target.
The official Ukrainian presidential releases support the infrastructure-protection context but do not independently prove the newly alleged Russian doctrine.
No immediate Philippine fuel-price effect is claimed.
The licensed photograph is a contextual 2023 image of Kyiv and is not presented as documentary evidence of the October 2026 events.
A repository and CMS search found no existing article with this slug or central event. The September 16 energy-strikes report is linked as the earliest relevant FMB News coverage.
